note:
#4701 is a CODE-QUALITY report, not a correctness one: nothing dxc emits here is wrong, the complaint is that a provably dead groupshared array survives optimisation. So the predicate does not test pass/fail; it counts two structural facts in the FINAL DXIL disassembly that the reporter explicitly asked to see removed ('Expect the store and the global variable to be removed'). Both are fixed in expected.md before anything was run.

Clause 3 (G >= 1): a module-level global of type [10 x float] in address space 3 survives. Address space 3 is TGSM/groupshared. This is 'the global variable' of the report.

Clause 4 (S >= 1): a store instruction whose pointer operand is in address space 3 survives. This is 'the store' of the report. Written structurally -- 'store float <anything>, float addrspace(3)*' -- rather than quoting the reporter's exact constant and getelementptr, so that a release which folds the GEP differently still scores. LLVM 3.7 typed-pointer syntax is used by every DXC release, so 'float addrspace(3)*' is portable; verified by hand against v1.4.1907, the bisection floor, which spells the whole line identically to today's build.

Clauses 1 and 2 are anti-vacuity anchors. Both symptom clauses are PRESENCE clauses, so a failed compile cannot satisfy them -- but a compile that emitted no DXIL at all also cannot be told from an optimised one without an anchor, and '!dx.entryPoints =' is emitted by every DXC release from v1.4.1907 onward only when a real module was produced. Exit 0 is the cheap second guard: on Windows dxc returns E_FAIL (0x80004005) for ordinary diagnosed errors, so a nonzero exit here means the probe measured nothing.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE PREDICATE: the PSV comment field 'NumBytesGroupSharedMemory: 40', which is the same finding in user-visible form (the compiled artifact reserves 40 bytes of group shared memory that no instruction ever reads). It is excluded because it is an INSTRUMENT that changed: v1.4.1907 does not print a PSVRuntimeInfo block at all, so a predicate keyed to it would score the bisection floor as clean and manufacture a regression. It is recorded as supplementary evidence in notes.md instead.

CONTROLS, all captured as variant-*.txt in this directory and all run through cmd.txt's exact arguments:
  control-static.hlsl   (--expect no-match)  the REFERENCE CASE: identical source with `static` in place of `groupshared`. dxc removes the array and the store entirely -- `define void @main() { ret void }` -- so the predicate does not fire. This is the input known to be good, and it is what makes 'the predicate matches everywhere' distinguishable from 'the bug is everywhere'.
  control-local.hlsl    (--expect no-match)  the same dead array as a function local; also fully removed.
  control-hello.hlsl    (--expect no-match)  a trivial cs_6_0 shader with a UAV store and no array; proves the predicate does not fire on just any clean compile, and doubles as the feature-presence probe that separates 'this release rejected my repro' from 'this release optimised it'.
  control-gs-live.hlsl  (--expect MATCH)     INSTRUMENT SELF-TEST: a groupshared array that is genuinely read back, so the allocation and the addrspace(3) store must legitimately survive. Its --expect is match, not no-match, on purpose: it is the positive control that proves clauses 3 and 4 can still see a groupshared global and an addrspace(3) store on the release under test. If it ever fails to match, that release is unmeasurable under this predicate rather than clean.

See match-deadarray.json for the address-space-agnostic twin used to measure the repro and the reference case on every release with one shared instrument.
